subject: Initial recap & next steps — Dedicated capacity fit for FinAnalytics
messages:
From: Adam Reynolds <adam.reynolds@finanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@finanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Intro — FinAnalytics inference profile and next steps

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick note to capture the high-level context from our side so we can align on capacity fit: 

- Primary workload: real-time scoring for risk models (microsecond-ish inference targets on single requests, bursty during market opens)
- Current stack: in-house TF/ONNX endpoints on heterogeneous GPU fleet; orchestrated with K8s and a homegrown queuing layer
- Pain: unpredictable tail latency during spikes, high unit cost when autoscaling to handle transient bursts, and security requirement to isolate ML inference for PII-tagged models
- Success criteria: sustained 500 TPS with p50 latency < 60ms, 99th < 250ms, predictable monthly bill within 10% variance, and SOC2-compatible auditability

I'll attach the monthly token/request snapshot we promised — hope that helps with sizing. Curious on your recommendation for reserved pools vs. a hybrid model (reserved + burst). Also please include what telemetry/data you'd need from our side to validate performance in a pilot.

Best,
Adam
Director of ML Engineering
FinAnalytics

Attachments: finanalytics-token-usage-snapshot.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Adam Reynolds <adam.reynolds@finanalytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — FinAnalytics inference profile and next steps

Adam — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the snapshot. Appreciate the latency and variance goals; that gives us a concrete target. High level takeaways from our side after reviewing: 

- Fit: Dedicated reserved GPU pools look appropriate given the isolation + predictable throughput requirement. A hybrid approach (reserved baseline + short-lived burst capacity) is often best for market-open spikes.
- Sizing notes: based on the CSV sample, rough estimate is a baseline pool sized for ~300 sustained TPS with an autoscale/burst policy that can add ~250 TPS for short windows (we'll confirm after more telemetry).
- Isolation & compliance: Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated with dedicated tenant/networking will meet SOC2/audit requirements; we can provide the required logs and KMS integration options.
- Telemetry we need: representative p50/p95/p99 request latencies with payload sizes, distribution of sequence lengths, and a short trace sample for tail requests. If you can share a 48–72 hour perf dump (anonymized), we can produce a more precise pool recommendation.

Next suggested steps:
1) Technical discovery with Marcus (solutions) to validate throughput assumptions and confirm autoscale thresholds — 60 minutes
2) Security/compliance sync to run through evidence list (SOC2 artifacts, EDR/KMS questions) — 30 minutes (can be combined)
3) Proposal for a 6-week pilot (reserved pool + telemetry/observability) with acceptance criteria aligned to your success metrics

Proposed times: Wed 8/19 10:00am PT (Marcus + Laura + me) or Thu 8/20 2:00pm PT. Which works for you?

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: Redwood capacity-fit checklist (we will share post-call)

From: Adam Reynolds <adam.reynolds@finanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@finanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — FinAnalytics inference profile and next steps

Soojin — Wed 8/19 10:00am PT works for us. Marcus, Laura — please consider this the invite hold.

A few clarifications before the call: 
- The 500 TPS target is an upper bound during peak events; our realistic sustained target for go-live is 350 TPS. We should size the baseline for 350 TPS with burst to 500 for 15–30 minute windows.
- Tail latency: we're particularly concerned about p99 during batch replays and during concurrent eval jobs (internal). If you have specific recommendations for queuing or prefix caching, please bring them to the discovery.
- Compliance: I attached our security intake outline; procurement will want pricing bands for reserved pool tiers and a draft SOW if the pilot scope aligns.

Thanks — looking forward to the discovery.
Adam

Attachments: security-qsa-request.pdf (PDF, 28KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Adam Reynolds <adam.reynolds@finanalytics.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — FinAnalytics inference profile and next steps

Thanks Adam — holding Wed 8/19 10:00am PT on my calendar. For the discovery call I'll prepare: 
- A lean sizing model (baseline pool + burst policy) with expected p50/p95/p99 projections based on your CSV input
- Options for burst enforcement: queue depth caps vs. token-based throttles, and expected cost delta for a 30-minute burst at 500 TPS
- Quick checklist for telemetry ingestion (sample trace format, anonymization checklist) and a short runbook for pilot acceptance testing

Action items for Adam/prior to meeting:
- Share 48–72 hour anonymized perf traces (p50/p95/p99) and a sample of payload sizes
- Procurement: a single point of contact for SOW/contract redlines so we can include them in the pilot draft

See you Wed.
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference

On Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:00:00 -07:00, calendar invite will send; please join via the Redwood Zoom link in the invite.
